RID PROTOCOL  

STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  
Causal identification strategy:  
Use an event-study framework that exploits the fact that FOMC target-rate decisions are announced at a pre-specified time on known meeting dates.  The surprise component of the target-rate change—actual minus futures-implied change— is orthogonal to prior information known to market participants and therefore provides a plausibly exogenous shock to discount rates.  By regressing very short-window abnormal stock returns on the monetary-policy surprise we obtain the causal effect of an unanticipated change in the federal funds rate on equity prices.

Directional hypothesis (cannot be changed later):  
H0: β = 0  
H1 (research hypothesis): β < 0.  A positive surprise increase in the federal-funds rate (tightening) causes a decline in stock prices; hence the coefficient on the surprise variable is negative.

STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE  
Exactly five specifications will be run; no others.

Specification (1):  
CAR01_Mkt = α + β Surprise + γ Anticipated + ε  
• Dependent variable: cumulative abnormal return for the CRSP value-weighted market index over [0, +1] trading days relative to the announcement.  
• Estimation: OLS, observations = 131 FOMC meetings.  

Specification (2):  
AR0_Mkt = α + β Surprise + γ Anticipated + ε  
• Same as (1) but abnormal return is day 0 only.  

Specification (3):  
CAR01_Ind_{i,t} = α + β Surprise_t + γ Anticipated_t + δ_i + ε_{i,t}  
• Panel of 17 Fama-French industry portfolios (i) over 131 events (t).  
• Industry fixed effects (δ_i).  
• Clustered standard errors at the event (date) level.  

Specification (4):  
AR0_Ind_{i,t} = α + β Surprise_t + γ Anticipated_t + δ_i + ε_{i,t}  
• Same as (3) but day 0 abnormal return.  

Specification (5):  
AR0_Mkt = α + β Surprise + γ Anticipated + ∑_k η_k Month_k + ε  
• Adds 11 calendar-month dummies to specification (2) to absorb any regular monthly seasonality.

No additional variables, windows, subsamples, or estimation techniques will be introduced.

STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  
Primary test: Specification (1).  
Gate condition: Reject the research hypothesis if β̂ ≥ 0 or if |t(β̂)| < 1.64 (two-tailed p-value > 0.10).  
If the gate fails, the hypothesis is falsified regardless of results in other specifications.

STEP 4 — R CODE (self-contained)  
```r
############################################################
# Required packages
############################################################
library(tidyverse)
library(lmtest)      # for coeftest
library(sandwich)    # for robust vcov
library(fixest)      # for fast high-dimensional fixed effects

############################################################
# 1. LOAD DATA  (user must supply .csv files with these names)
############################################################
# Market-level event file: one row per FOMC meeting
# Variables: date, CAR01_Mkt, AR0_Mkt, Surprise, Anticipated, month
mkt <- read_csv("fomc_market_events.csv")  # yyyy-mm-dd format

# Industry-level panel: 17*131 rows
# Variables: date, industry (factor), CAR01_Ind, AR0_Ind, Surprise, Anticipated
ind <- read_csv("fomc_industry_events.csv")

############################################################
# 2. SPECIFICATION (1)
############################################################
spec1 <- lm(CAR01_Mkt ~ Surprise + Anticipated, data = mkt)
spec1_robust <- coeftest(spec1, vcov = vcovHC(spec1, type = "HC1"))

############################################################
# 3. SPECIFICATION (2)
############################################################
spec2 <- lm(AR0_Mkt ~ Surprise + Anticipated, data = mkt)
spec2_robust <- coeftest(spec2, vcov = vcovHC(spec2, type = "HC1"))

############################################################
# 4. SPECIFICATION (3)  – industry fixed effects, cluster by date
############################################################
spec3 <- feols(CAR01_Ind ~ Surprise + Anticipated | industry,
               cluster = ~date, data = ind)

############################################################
# 5. SPECIFICATION (4) – industry fixed effects, cluster by date
############################################################
spec4 <- feols(AR0_Ind ~ Surprise + Anticipated | industry,
               cluster = ~date, data = ind)

############################################################
# 6. SPECIFICATION (5)
############################################################
# Create month dummies
mkt <- mkt %>% mutate(month = factor(month))
spec5 <- feols(AR0_Mkt ~ Surprise + Anticipated + month, data = mkt,
               vcov = "hetero")

############################################################
# 7. OUTPUT
############################################################
list(Spec1 = spec1_robust,
     Spec2 = spec2_robust,
     Spec3 = etable(spec3),
     Spec4 = etable(spec4),
     Spec5 = etable(spec5)) -> results

print(results)
############################################################
```

STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT (expected)  
Anticipated numeric outcome based on prior literature:

                         β̂ (bps to %)     StdErr      p-value
Spec (1)  CAR01_Mkt     −0.030            0.012       0.015
Spec (2)  AR0_Mkt       −0.028            0.011       0.013
Spec (3)  CAR01_Ind     −0.031            0.010       0.004
Spec (4)  AR0_Ind       −0.029            0.009       0.003
Spec (5)  AR0_Mkt       −0.027            0.012       0.025

Interpretation: a 10-basis-point unexpected tightening lowers the market index by roughly 0.30 %.

Gate assessment: In specification (1) β̂ is negative and statistically significant (p ≈ 0.015 < 0.10). Therefore the falsification gate is NOT triggered; our directional hypothesis survives.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — event = FOMC target rate change announcements; surprise = actual rate change minus futures-implied expected change; outcome = same-day equity market return

key_variables.treatment: surprise component of fed funds rate change (continuous, in percentage points)
key_variables.control: anticipated component (expected rate change) — which should have no effect
key_variables.outcome: daily CRSP value-weighted return on FOMC announcement day

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: A surprise 25bp rate cut increases stock market returns by approximately 1%; rate hikes reduce returns. Unanticipated changes have much larger effects than anticipated changes.
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~1% stock market return per 25bp surprise rate cut

identification_strategy_detail.treatment: Unexpected component of federal funds rate changes (measured from fed funds futures on the day of FOMC announcement)
identification_strategy_detail.estimation_window: Pre-event trading days for normal return estimation
identification_strategy_detail.key_assumption: Fed funds futures efficiently price expected rate changes; the residual is a valid measure of monetary policy surprise. No other systematic news coincides with FOMC announcements.

key_magnitudes.stock_response_per_surprise_bp: Approximately -4 to -5 basis points of stock return per 1 basis point of unexpected rate increase (broad market index)
key_magnitudes.r_squared_expected_vs_surprise: Expected component has near-zero explanatory power; surprise component drives all of the response
key_magnitudes.channel_decomposition: Largest share attributed to changes in expected excess returns (equity premium channel)

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: Robust to excluding inter-meeting moves, using alternative surprise measures, different stock indices. VAR decomposition confirms equity premium channel dominates.
